clean.name: Hips shoot up off the floor
clean.looks_like: Right after the bar breaks the floor the hips rise fast while the bar and shoulders barely move; back angle tips toward horizontal.
root_causes: rushing/yanking the bar off the floor with slack in the body
quads weak at small knee angles relative to hips
believing the back angle must change
clean.downstream_effect: Balance shifts forward onto toes, early second pull, lower bar speed and height, bar swings forward later.
clean.signal: Trunk angle (hip->shoulder vs horizontal) change and hip vs shoulder vertical rise between bar lift-off and bar at knee height. Ratio hip_rise/shoulder_rise from keypoints; bar height from plate centre.

threshold.value: trunk angle drops >15 deg toward horizontal before bar reaches knee, OR hip_rise/shoulder_rise >1.5 over floor-to-knee
threshold.source: heuristic; Catalyst says back angle should stay 'fairly constant' (no number)

cues: Push the floor away with your legs
Keep your back angle off the floor
Squeeze the slack out before you pull
Lift your chest as the bar leaves
Smooth off the floor, then faster
why: Pull speed is bar speed: hips racing up while the bar stalls makes the pull slower, not faster.
Keeping the back angle lets the legs do the first pull so the hips are saved for the second.
drills: Pause clean deadlift (just off floor and at knee)

clean.name: Bar drifts forward off the floor
clean.looks_like: Plate moves away from the shins/toes instead of straight up or slightly back toward the lifter.
root_causes: weight shifts onto toes before bar passes knee
clean.downstream_effect: Lifter chases the bar forward, second pull pushes it further away, jump forward, missed catch in front.
clean.signal: Bar (plate centre) horizontal displacement relative to its start x, from lift-off until bar passes knee height. Scale px->cm via 45 cm plate diameter.

threshold.value: bar >3 cm forward of start x at knee height (ideal: 0 to slightly back)
threshold.source: heuristic; Kuhn 2001 measured first-pull horizontal displacement -3 to +8 cm (women, snatch); Petrizzo 2016 start tweak cut clean HD ~3.2 cm

cues: Sweep the bar back to your shins
Keep the bar brushing your legs
Weight to mid-foot as it rises
Pull the bar into you, not up
Let the knees move out of the way
why: Every centimetre the bar travels forward has to be pulled back later, usually by jumping forward or catching out front.

clean.name: Bar too far forward at setup
clean.looks_like: In the start position the bar sits over the toes with steep shins; ankle angle small.
root_causes: setting up with bar away from shins
clean.downstream_effect: Forces the bar forward in the first pull; bar lifted too far from the body.
clean.signal: Bar x at rest vs ankle and toe keypoints (foot keypoints noisy). Shin angle (knee->ankle) at setup.

threshold.value: bar x more than ~4 cm ahead of the ball-of-foot estimate (ankle x + 0.6 * foot length); QWA: ankle angle should not go below ~60-70 deg
threshold.source: QWA (ankle angle 60-70 deg); bar-over-foot offset is heuristic

cues: Bar over the balls of your feet
Shoulders just ahead of the bar
Set the bar closer before you pull
why: Starting closer means the bar doesn't have to be dragged back mid-pull.

clean.name: Shoulders behind the bar too early
clean.looks_like: Torso becomes upright while the bar is still at or just above the knees; shoulders behind the bar before the hips are reached.
root_causes: impatience to start the second pull
weak hamstrings/back in the over-bar position
clean.downstream_effect: Bar hits or swings around the knees, early arm bend, weak and short second pull, bar looped forward.
clean.signal: Shoulder keypoint x vs bar x while bar is between knee and mid-thigh (mid-thigh = midpoint of knee and hip keypoints).

threshold.value: shoulder >5 cm behind bar x before bar reaches mid-thigh
threshold.source: heuristic; Catalyst: shoulders over/slightly ahead of bar until mid-to-upper thigh

cues: Shoulders over the bar to mid-thigh
Push with the legs, don't lean back
Bar to the hips before you open
Keep your chest over the bar
why: Opening early spends hip extension before the bar is in position, so the explosion happens with the bar low on the thigh.
drills: Segment clean (pause at knee and mid-thigh)

clean.name: Bar swings around or hits the knees
clean.looks_like: Bar path bows forward around knee height, or the lifter's knees clip the bar.
root_causes: knees not moved back during first pull
bar too far back at start / dragging
clean.downstream_effect: Bar loses speed, path bends forward, timing breaks.
clean.signal: Local forward bulge of bar x around knee keypoint height; abrupt vertical deceleration of bar near knee (contact).

threshold.value: forward bulge >3 cm around knee height or bar vertical velocity dropping >30% for <100 ms at knee height
threshold.source: heuristic

cues: Knees back as the bar rises
Let the bar hang from straight arms
Move your knees, not the bar
why: Knees need to move back so the bar can travel straight; swinging around them adds a forward loop.

clean.name: Jumping from too low on the thigh
clean.looks_like: Explosive hip extension starts with the bar at or just above the knee instead of upper thigh/hip.
clean.downstream_effect: Bar is hit forward off the thigh, power is wasted, forward jump.
clean.signal: Timing of peak hip-angle extension velocity vs bar height. Bar height normalised between knee (0) and hip (1) keypoints at that frame.

threshold.value: peak hip extension velocity occurs with bar <0.6 of knee-to-hip distance (aim 0.8-1.0, upper thigh/hip)
threshold.source: heuristic; Garza (Catalyst) says jump only once bar reaches hip 'explode' position

cues: Wait for the bar at your hips
Bar high on the thigh first
why: The legs and hips are strongest pushing upward once the bar is high on the thigh; starting earlier pushes it forward.

clean.name: Bar swings away after hip contact
clean.looks_like: After the hips/thighs contact the bar, the plate arcs forward away from the body before the catch (big forward loop).
root_causes: hips thrust forward instead of up
clean.downstream_effect: Lifter must jump forward to catch, bar received in front, chest drops, misses forward.
clean.signal: Bar x forward excursion from its most-rearward point (around hip contact) to max forward point before rack. Plate-calibrated cm.

threshold.value: forward excursion >6 cm (heavier lifters/taller allow ~+2 cm); >10 cm almost always a miss risk
threshold.source: heuristic; Kuhn 2001 reported -14 to +14 cm in second pull, -3 to +21 cm after peak (women snatch); no clean-specific cutoff found

cues: Keep the bar close after contact
Brush the bar, don't bang it
Drive straight up through the floor
Pull yourself under, bar stays home
why: The bar should travel up and slightly back; thrusting the hips forward hits it out in front.
Elbows lifting up and out keep the bar close while you pull under.

clean.name: Cutting the pull short
clean.looks_like: Lifter starts dropping under before hips and knees straighten; never reaches tall, slightly-back finish.
clean.downstream_effect: Low bar height and speed, crash on the shoulders, weak power cleans.
clean.signal: Max hip angle (shoulder-hip-knee) and max knee angle (hip-knee-ankle) reached before hip vertical velocity turns negative. Also bar peak vertical velocity.

threshold.value: max hip angle <160 deg OR max knee angle <155 deg before descent (full extension ~175-180 deg; margin for 10 deg error)
threshold.source: heuristic; QWA and CrossFit L1 list incomplete extension as a fault but give no angle

cues: Stand all the way up fast
Push the floor until you're tall
why: The bar gets most of its upward speed in the last few centimetres of extension; skipping it leaves the bar low.

clean.name: Bending the arms early
clean.looks_like: Elbows visibly bend while the bar is still below the hips, like an upright row into the hips.
clean.downstream_effect: Bar crashes on shoulders, force leaks through bent elbows, slow third pull, bar pulled backward.
clean.signal: Elbow angle (shoulder-elbow-wrist) while bar is below hip keypoint height (before peak extension).

threshold.value: elbow angle <150 deg while bar below hip height (straight ~170-180 deg; margin for 10 deg error)
threshold.source: heuristic; PLT4M/Catalyst: arms bend only after hip extension

cues: Arms are ropes, legs do it
Relax your arms in the pull
why: Bent arms soak up the leg drive; the arms only connect the bar to the body until extension is done.

clean.name: Leaning back too far at the finish
clean.looks_like: At peak extension the torso is far behind vertical, shoulders well behind hips.
clean.downstream_effect: Bar pulled backward, lifter falls/jumps back, slow pull-under.
clean.signal: Trunk angle vs vertical at peak extension (hip->shoulder).

threshold.value: trunk >25 deg behind vertical at peak extension
threshold.source: heuristic

cues: Shoulders over hips at the top
why: Leaning back moves the bar backward and makes you travel farther to get under.

clean.name: Jumping forward
clean.looks_like: Feet land noticeably in front of where they started.
root_causes: no sweep back in first pull
bar swings forward and lifter chases it
clean.downstream_effect: Catch in front, chest collapse, missed or unstable clean.
clean.signal: Ankle/toe keypoint x at landing vs start x (median of standing frames). Plate gives cm scale.

threshold.value: feet land >5 cm forward of start
threshold.source: heuristic; Everett notes common forward jump of ~3 in (7.6 cm) and coach-mat correction; overcorrect by jumping back ~0.5 in

cues: Stay over your heels at the top
why: Your feet go where the bar went: landing forward means the bar went forward.
drills: Coach mat / tape line in front of toes

clean.name: Feet kick back / land far behind
clean.looks_like: Feet land well behind start or one kicks back (donkey kick).
clean.downstream_effect: Lifter falls backward in the catch, unstable recovery.
clean.signal: Ankle/toe x at landing vs start.

threshold.value: feet land >8 cm behind start
threshold.source: heuristic

why: Some small backward jump is fine; a big one means the bar went too far back.

clean.name: Slow pull-under / turnover
clean.looks_like: Long gap between full extension and the bar landing in the rack; lifter seems to wait then drop.
clean.downstream_effect: Bar crashes, lifter caught out of position, harder recovery and jerk.
clean.signal: Time from peak extension (max hip angle frame) to rack fixation (bar vertical velocity ~0 and bar within ~8 cm of shoulder keypoint). Needs >=60 fps.

threshold.value: turnover >0.45 s (snatch literature drop-under ~0.30-0.38 s)
threshold.source: heuristic from snatch drop-under times (Kuhn et al. literature review); no clean-specific number

cues: Don't wait for it, go get it
why: The bar is only weightless for a fraction of a second; get under before it starts falling.

clean.name: Bar crashes onto the shoulders
clean.looks_like: Bar falls a long way and slams into the shoulders; elbows/torso jolt down at impact.
root_causes: dropping straight down instead of meeting the bar
clean.downstream_effect: Loss of rack, collapse, sternum/clavicle pain, missed recovery.
clean.signal: Bar drop: bar max height minus bar height at rack contact; bar downward velocity at the contact frame relative to the shoulder keypoint.

threshold.value: bar drop >12 cm from peak to rack, or bar-minus-shoulder downward velocity >0.8 m/s at contact
threshold.source: heuristic; 2019 elite snatch study: smaller catch-phase drop separated successful lifts; women snatch average drop 20.8 cm

cues: Meet the bar where it is
Catch it high and ride it
why: A bar that falls far gathers speed; meeting it early means you absorb less.

clean.name: Low elbows in the catch
clean.looks_like: Elbows point down at the floor, bar rolling forward off the shoulders.
clean.downstream_effect: Bar rolls forward, chest drops, elbows hit knees, missed recovery.
clean.signal: Upper-arm angle (shoulder->elbow) vs horizontal at rack fixation; elbow often occluded by knee in deep squat.

threshold.value: upper arm >45 deg below horizontal at catch
threshold.source: heuristic

cues: Lift your elbows to the wall
Shoulders up, bar in the shelf
why: High elbows keep the torso upright and the bar on the shoulders, not in the hands.

clean.name: Elbows touch knees
clean.looks_like: In the bottom, elbows rest on or hit the thighs/knees.
clean.downstream_effect: No lift in competition (IWF), injury risk, collapse.
clean.signal: Elbow keypoint distance to knee keypoint at the bottom of the squat clean (frequent occlusion).

threshold.value: elbow-knee distance <5 cm at bottom
threshold.source: heuristic (joint error ~5 cm limits reliability)

cues: Get the bar on your shoulders
why: Elbow-knee contact means the torso has folded; it's also a red light.

clean.name: Chest collapses forward in the catch
clean.looks_like: Torso pitches forward in the receive; bar ends up over the toes.
clean.downstream_effect: Bar dumped in front, good-morning recovery, missed clean.
clean.signal: Trunk angle vs vertical at the lowest hip frame; bar x vs mid-foot (ankle + 0.4 * foot length).

threshold.value: trunk >45 deg from vertical, OR bar >8 cm ahead of mid-foot in the receive
threshold.source: heuristic

why: An upright torso keeps the bar over your feet so your legs can stand it up.

clean.name: Power clean received below parallel
clean.looks_like: Intended power clean but hip crease drops below the knee (turns into a squat clean).
root_causes: load too heavy for a power
clean.downstream_effect: Not a power clean by definition; informative for load selection.
clean.signal: Hip keypoint y vs knee keypoint y at the lowest point (hip below knee = below parallel).

threshold.value: hip y below knee y (thighs below horizontal) when variant=power
threshold.source: Everett: power clean = received with thighs above horizontal

why: Power cleans train a higher pull; if you have to squat it, the pull or load is off.

clean.name: Catch high then fall into the squat
clean.looks_like: Lifter lands in a partial squat, stops, then drops into the full squat (two-stage receive).
root_causes: bar too low for a power
clean.downstream_effect: Bar crashes on the second drop; loses elastic rebound.
clean.signal: Hip vertical position/velocity during the receive: two distinct descent phases separated by a near-zero-velocity pause >80 ms.

threshold.value: pause >80 ms between two descending hip phases
threshold.source: heuristic

cues: Ride it all the way down
Feet down, then sit straight in
why: One continuous ride lets you absorb the bar and use the bounce; stopping halfway lets it crash.

clean.name: Catching on the toes
clean.looks_like: Heels stay off the floor in the receive; weight on balls of the feet.
clean.downstream_effect: Forward instability, collapse.
clean.signal: Heel keypoint (if model has it) height above floor vs toe keypoint at the receive.

threshold.value: heel >3 cm above floor at rack fixation
threshold.source: heuristic (foot keypoints noisy)

why: Full-foot contact gives a stable base to stand the bar up.

clean.name: Hips rise first out of the squat
clean.looks_like: Coming up from the bottom, hips rise faster than shoulders (good-morning recovery).
clean.downstream_effect: Bar rolls forward, missed recovery, tired for the jerk.
clean.signal: Trunk angle change and hip vs shoulder rise during first 1/3 of recovery.

threshold.value: trunk angle tips >15 deg forward during first third of recovery
threshold.source: heuristic; squat literature notes small change is normal

cues: Stay tall out of the hole
why: Letting the hips lead turns a squat into a good morning and pulls the bar forward.

clean.name: Bar drifts forward in recovery
clean.looks_like: While standing up, the bar moves ahead of mid-foot and the lifter steps forward.
clean.downstream_effect: Stumbles, missed clean, bad jerk setup.
clean.signal: Bar x vs mid-foot during recovery; any ankle x step.

threshold.value: bar >8 cm ahead of mid-foot or a forward step >10 cm during recovery
threshold.source: heuristic

why: The bar should rise vertically over your feet so the legs, not the back, finish it.

clean.name: Bar pulled excessively backward
clean.looks_like: Bar travels far behind the start line and lifter falls back in the catch.
clean.downstream_effect: Falls backward, misses behind.
clean.signal: Bar x at catch relative to start x.

threshold.value: bar >10 cm behind start x at rack fixation AND lifter steps back
threshold.source: heuristic; Kuhn ranges -3 to -14 cm in snatch

why: A little backward travel is normal; too much drags you off balance.

clean.name: Hang: no knee rebend (RDL hang)
clean.looks_like: From the hang, the lifter hinges with locked knees then swings the hips; knees never come forward under the bar.
clean.downstream_effect: Weak drive, bar banged forward with hips, early arm pull.
clean.signal: Knee angle at the bottom of the hang countermovement; hip x movement during the countermovement.

threshold.value: knee angle >165 deg at bottom of hang countermovement
threshold.source: heuristic

why: The legs need a bend to push from; locked knees leave only a hip swing.
drills: Hang clean from mid-thigh with pause

clean.name: Hang: shoulders behind the bar
clean.looks_like: In the hang position the torso is upright and shoulders are behind the bar before the jump.
clean.downstream_effect: Hips can't load; bar swung forward; early arm bend.
clean.signal: Shoulder keypoint x vs bar x in the hang (static frames before jump).

threshold.value: shoulder >4 cm behind bar x in hang
threshold.source: heuristic

cues: Bar on your thighs, chest over
why: Shoulders over the bar let the hips extend into the bar instead of hitting it away.

clean.name: Not enough bar height
clean.looks_like: Bar barely rises above the belt before the lifter has to receive it.
clean.downstream_effect: Deep crash, missed power cleans.
clean.signal: Bar peak height normalised by lifter height H (standing frame or plate-scaled).

threshold.value: power clean bar peak <0.58 H (literature clean displacement ~55-65% of height)
threshold.source: Costley summary of Garhammer/Winchester/Storey (unverified secondary)

why: Bar height comes from finishing the extension, not from the arms.

clean.name: Rounded back at setup
clean.looks_like: Upper or lower back flexes in the start or as the bar leaves the floor.
clean.downstream_effect: Hips rise first, load on lower back, bar forward.
clean.signal: Only gross check: shoulder-hip-ear alignment; spine curvature is not captured by keypoints.

threshold.value: none found
threshold.source: none found

why: A rounded back leaks force and makes the hips shoot up.

clean.name: Feet land too wide or narrow
clean.looks_like: Feet slam out much wider than squat stance, or stay narrow.
clean.downstream_effect: Unstable bottom, knee strain.
clean.signal: Front view needed; side-on cannot see width.

threshold.value: none found
threshold.source: none found

why: The catch stance should match your front squat stance.

jerk.name: Chest drops / torso tips in the dip
jerk.looks_like: Torso pitches forward during the dip; bar moves ahead of the shoulders.
root_causes: hinging at hips instead of knees
jerk.downstream_effect: Bar driven forward, lifter chases it, missed jerk forward.
jerk.signal: Trunk angle (hip->shoulder) vs vertical: change from rack stance to bottom of dip.

threshold.value: trunk tips >12 deg forward of its rack-stance angle at dip bottom
threshold.source: heuristic; Catalyst/QWA require an upright trunk but give no angle

why: Any forward tilt in the dip turns into a forward bar path in the drive.

jerk.name: Hips push back in the dip
jerk.looks_like: The dip looks like a hinge: butt sticks back, knees stay behind.
jerk.downstream_effect: Bar falls forward off the shoulders, forward drive.
jerk.signal: Hip keypoint x shift relative to ankle x from stance to dip bottom (backwards = fault).

threshold.value: hip moves >5 cm backward during the dip
threshold.source: heuristic; Catalyst: dip is knees only, no hips

why: Hinging tips the torso and the bar falls forward; a knee-only dip keeps the bar over the feet.
drills: Jerk dip with back against wall

jerk.name: Dip too deep
jerk.looks_like: Bar sinks far, often slowly; looks like a quarter squat or deeper.
jerk.downstream_effect: Leg drive fades out of the bottom, low bar height, torso collapse.
jerk.signal: Bar vertical drop from rack height to lowest dip point, normalised by lifter height H (from standing frame keypoints or plate scale).

threshold.value: >13% of height (coaching range 8-12%; Soviet ~11%)
threshold.source: Soviet data via Breaking Muscle (~11% H), Catalyst ~10%, Encyclopedia 8-12%; Grabe & Widule 1988 ~13% (secondary)

why: Beyond about a tenth of your height, the legs stop adding speed and the torso starts to sag.

jerk.name: Dip too shallow
jerk.looks_like: Barely any knee bend before the drive; almost a press.
jerk.downstream_effect: Not enough leg drive, bar doesn't reach lockout height, press out.
jerk.signal: Same dip-depth signal as above.

threshold.value: <6% of height
threshold.source: heuristic below the 8-12% coaching range

why: The dip loads the legs like a spring; too little and the arms have to do it.

jerk.name: Slow dip or pause at the bottom
jerk.looks_like: Lifter sinks slowly or stops at the bottom before driving.
jerk.downstream_effect: Loses stretch reflex and bar whip, forces more arm work, press out.
jerk.signal: Dip duration (rack to bottom) and time at bar vertical velocity ~0 (<0.05 m/s) at the bottom. Needs >=60 fps.

threshold.value: bottom pause >0.10 s or dip duration >0.5 s (Soviet: ~0.3 s accel + ~0.1 s brake, pause 0.03-0.06 s)
threshold.source: Soviet timings via Breaking Muscle (secondary)

why: The bar flexes and your legs stretch in the dip; pausing wastes both.

jerk.name: Bar leaves the shoulders / elbows drop
jerk.looks_like: Bar separates from the shoulders or elbows sag during the dip.
root_causes: bar resting on top of shoulders
jerk.downstream_effect: Drive force leaks, bar forward.
jerk.signal: Vertical gap between bar and shoulder keypoint during dip; elbow keypoint drop relative to shoulder.

threshold.value: bar-shoulder gap increases >4 cm or elbow drops >5 cm relative to shoulder during dip
threshold.source: heuristic

cues: Keep the bar on your shoulders
why: The bar must move with your body in the dip, or the drive hits empty air.

jerk.name: Dipping or driving on the toes
jerk.looks_like: Heels rise during the dip or before the drive finishes.
jerk.downstream_effect: Forward drive and short split.
jerk.signal: Heel keypoint height during dip and early drive vs standing.

threshold.value: heel >2 cm above floor before knee angle reaches ~160 deg in drive
threshold.source: heuristic

why: Rising onto the toes early tips your balance forward and pushes the bar forward.

jerk.name: Bar driven forward
jerk.looks_like: Bar travels forward of the rack position rather than straight up or slightly back.
jerk.downstream_effect: Lifter must chase it; bar lands in front; missed jerk (most common elite miss per Sportivny/Prassas).
jerk.signal: Bar x from rack start to lockout, plate-calibrated; also lockout bar x vs rack x.

threshold.value: bar ends >3 cm forward of rack x (Catalyst: path should go slightly back)
threshold.source: heuristic; Prassas & Fulton 1994: failed lift had substantially more forward bar travel (no cm)

cues: Drive it back over your head
Push the bar behind your ears
Get your face out of the way
why: A straight-up bar is already too far forward; aim slightly back so it lands over the base.

jerk.name: Bar locked out in front of the base
jerk.looks_like: At lockout the bar is ahead of the lifter's base of support, over the front foot or toes.
jerk.downstream_effect: Bar falls forward, steps, misses.
jerk.signal: Bar x at lockout vs base centre: split = midpoint of front ankle and back toe (approx); power/push = mid-foot.

threshold.value: bar >8 cm ahead of base centre at lockout
threshold.source: heuristic; Everett: bar over mid-to-rear foot

why: Only a bar over your base is stable; anything in front pulls you after it.

jerk.name: Head not through
jerk.looks_like: At lockout the bar is in front of the face/ear line; head not pushed through the arms.
root_causes: not pulling head back during drive
jerk.downstream_effect: Weak overhead support, forward miss.
jerk.signal: Bar x at lockout vs ear (or nose) keypoint x.

threshold.value: bar >3 cm ahead of ear keypoint at lockout
threshold.source: heuristic; Everett/Invictus: bar behind ears

cues: Pull the head back, then through
why: Moving your head out of the way lets the bar go straight up, then you push it back over your spine.

jerk.name: Pressing before the legs finish
jerk.looks_like: Elbows start extending while knees are still bent in the drive.
jerk.downstream_effect: Low bar height, slow drop, press out.
jerk.signal: Timing: elbow angle increase >20 deg before knee angle reaches ~165 deg in the drive.

threshold.value: elbow extension >20 deg before knee reaches 165 deg
threshold.source: heuristic; Catalyst: elastic jerkers engage arms earlier, so style-dependent

why: The legs should launch the bar; the arms push you under it.

jerk.name: Weak drive / low bar height
jerk.looks_like: Bar barely lifts off the shoulders before the lifter drops; catches very low.
jerk.downstream_effect: Lifter drops too low into split, press out.
jerk.signal: Bar rise from dip bottom to peak, normalised by H; bar peak vertical velocity.

threshold.value: bar rise from dip bottom to peak <12% of height
threshold.source: heuristic; Grabe & Widule ~18% H vertical bar displacement (secondary)

why: Every centimetre of drive is a centimetre you don't have to drop.

jerk.name: Press out
jerk.looks_like: Arms keep extending after the lifter has reached the low point of the split/squat.
jerk.downstream_effect: No lift under IWF rules; unstable lockout.
jerk.signal: Elbow angle at frame of lowest hip position vs max elbow angle afterwards.

threshold.value: elbow angle rises >12 deg after lowest hip point (rule: any pressing after low point is a fault; margin for 10 deg error)
threshold.source: IWF rule 2.5.1.4 (via SportsEdTV); numeric margin heuristic

cues: Punch and lock as you land
why: The arms should be locked as your feet land; pushing after that is a red light.

jerk.name: Elbows re-bend in recovery
jerk.looks_like: After lockout, an elbow softens then straightens again.
jerk.downstream_effect: No lift under IWF rules.
jerk.signal: Elbow angle drop after lockout then re-rise.

threshold.value: elbow drops >15 deg after lockout then re-extends
threshold.source: IWF rule 2.5.1.5 via Ironmind; numeric margin heuristic

why: Locked arms are steadier, and a re-bend is a red light.

jerk.name: Short split
jerk.looks_like: Feet barely separate; back knee under or ahead of the hips.
jerk.downstream_effect: Can't get under, bar forward, lifter pushed back/forward.
jerk.signal: Back knee keypoint x vs hip x in split; front ankle to back ankle distance / H.

threshold.value: back knee not >=5 cm behind hip x, OR ankle-to-ankle distance <0.35 H
threshold.source: Catalyst: back knee should be behind the hips; length ratio heuristic

cues: Step longer with the front foot
why: A longer split lets you drop under without falling forward or back.

jerk.name: Front knee forward of ankle
jerk.looks_like: Front shin angles forward with knee past the toes.
jerk.downstream_effect: Unstable, knee strain, bar forward.
jerk.signal: Front shin angle (knee->ankle) vs vertical in receive.

threshold.value: front shin >15 deg forward of vertical
threshold.source: Everett: shin vertical, knee over or slightly behind ankle; degree cutoff heuristic

cues: Heel down on the front foot
why: A vertical front shin braces against the forward push of the bar.

jerk.name: Over-stepping the split
jerk.looks_like: Front foot shoots very far; front shin leans back and hips drop very low.
root_causes: weak drive making lifter dive low
jerk.downstream_effect: Hard recovery, hips stuck behind.
jerk.signal: Front shin backward angle; front thigh angle to floor.

threshold.value: front shin >15 deg behind vertical OR front thigh <15 deg to floor (Everett 20-40 deg)
threshold.source: Everett 20-40 deg thigh angle; cutoff heuristic

why: Too long a split drops you lower than you need and makes recovery a struggle.

jerk.name: Straight back leg / too bent
jerk.looks_like: Back knee locked straight, or bent close to 90 deg with knee near floor.
jerk.downstream_effect: Locked: hyperextension, hips can't drop; bent: hips too low, unstable.
jerk.signal: Back knee angle (hip-knee-ankle) in receive.

threshold.value: >170 deg (locked) or <110 deg (too bent)
threshold.source: Everett: back knee bent; Catalyst: ~90 deg excessive; cutoffs heuristic

why: A slightly bent back knee keeps the heel up and lets the hips sit under the bar.

jerk.name: Front foot lands first
jerk.looks_like: Front foot hits noticeably before the back foot.
jerk.downstream_effect: Hips behind bar, bar forward.
jerk.signal: Foot contact frames (ankle vertical velocity ~0) for front and back feet; need >=60 fps.

threshold.value: front contact >50 ms before back contact
threshold.source: heuristic; Catalyst notes back foot should be slightly first but often imperceptible

why: Driving the back foot keeps the hips moving under the bar.

jerk.name: Hips stuck behind / diving forward
jerk.looks_like: In the split, torso leans forward and hips sit behind the bar.
root_causes: jerking from front changes torso position
jerk.downstream_effect: Bar ahead of base, lifter falls forward.
jerk.signal: Hip x vs bar x at lockout; trunk angle vs vertical.

threshold.value: hip >8 cm behind bar x OR trunk >15 deg forward at lockout
threshold.source: heuristic

why: Your hips need to land under the bar; diving forward leaves them behind.

jerk.name: Power/push jerk caught too deep
jerk.looks_like: Lifter drops into a half squat or deeper to catch.
jerk.downstream_effect: Hard recovery, unstable overhead.
jerk.signal: Min knee angle in receive.

threshold.value: knee angle <90 deg in receive (power jerk is typically partial squat)
threshold.source: heuristic; Torokhtiy describes power jerk catch as partial/half squat

cues: Lock it in a quarter squat
why: A deep power jerk usually means the drive was short.

jerk.name: Feet move in push jerk
jerk.looks_like: In a push jerk the feet leave the floor or slide.
jerk.downstream_effect: It's a power jerk; informational label.
jerk.signal: Ankle x displacement or ankle lift during receive.

threshold.value: ankle moves >5 cm or lifts >3 cm
threshold.source: heuristic

why: The push jerk keeps the feet still so you learn to drop with the knees.

jerk.name: Recovering back foot first
jerk.looks_like: From the split, the back foot steps forward first.
jerk.downstream_effect: Bar moves forward horizontally, unstable recovery.
jerk.signal: Order of ankle x motion after split stabilises.

threshold.value: back ankle moves >5 cm before front ankle moves
threshold.source: Catalyst recommends front foot first

cues: Bar stays still as you recover
why: Stepping the front foot back first keeps the bar over the strongest post.

jerk.name: Walking with the bar overhead
jerk.looks_like: Lifter shuffles or takes several steps to save the bar.
jerk.downstream_effect: Missed or ugly lift.
jerk.signal: Ankle x displacement total after first foot contact until stable.

threshold.value: >15 cm total foot travel after receive
threshold.source: heuristic

why: If you have to walk, the bar landed off the base.

jerk.name: Feet on a tightrope
jerk.looks_like: Feet line up like a tightrope, too narrow side-to-side.
jerk.downstream_effect: Lateral wobble.
jerk.signal: Front view needed.

threshold.value: none found (Everett: width ~squat stance)
threshold.source: Everett

why: Side-to-side width matters as much as length for balance.
drills: Step to split on tape lines

notes.scale: Use the 45 cm plate diameter for px->cm and standing-frame keypoints for lifter height H.
notes.pose_error_context: Theia3D vs Vicon in snatch: joint centres ~4.7-5.7 cm off, sagittal joint angles RMSD ~13.6 deg; thresholds include margins for that.
notes.verified_flag: verified=true only where the number comes from a primary rule/source; most thresholds are heuristic starting points to tune on the eval set.
